issues.title: API Retrieve Guestbook Responses for a Dataverse Collection in JSON format
issues.body:
When a sub-collection uses guestbooks inherited from its parent collection, we need to retrieve the guestbook responses using a specific Dataverse collection ID.

We have an api similarly but in csv format [Retrieve Guestbook Responses for a Dataverse Collection](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/api/native-api.html#id72) in Native API, but we also need return responses in JSON format.

Can we extend this API to support a Dataverse collection ID as well?
`curl -H  "X-Dataverse-key:$API_TOKEN" "$SERVER_URL/api/guestbooks/$ID/responses?limit10&offset=0"`

issues.title: Feature Request: Add Template APIs for SPA
issues.body:
**Overview of the Feature Request** 
SPA needs to be able to access the collection's list of dataset templates. Currently this is done through the ManageTemplatesPage and TemplatePage. There are no non-admin APIs to match this functionality. 

This feature aims to provide a set of new endpoints for listing, creating, editing, and managing templates directly through the API.

Native APIs:
GET list of templates /api/dataverses/{dataverseAlias}/templates
POST a new template /api/dataverses/{dataverseAlias}/template with json template object (requires Permission.EditDataverse)

Existing APIs
DELETE /admin/template/{id}
GET /admin/templates
GET /admin/templates/{alias}

New API Requests: 
- Edit template metadata: Updates the template’s metadata fields.
- Manage template terms: Allows adding and editing of the template’s terms section.
- Set a template as default: Marks the specified template as the default for the Dataverse.

(Example users roles: API User, Curator, Depositor, Guest, Superuser, Sysadmin)

issues.title: Feature Request/Idea: Export metadatablock definition per Dataverse collection
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to the Dataverse Project through the creation of a feature request!

More information on ideas/feature requests and contributions can be found in the "Contributing to Dataverse" page:
https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#ideasfeature-requests

Please fill out as much of the template as you can.
Start below this comment section.
-->

**Overview of the Feature Request**

Currently the Native API supports the export of an overview of metadatablocks and a detailed view using `.../metadatablocks` and `.../metadatablocks/$blockID` respectively. Same applies to Dataverse collections, but these are missing the detailed view. Hence, it would be a valuable addition to the Native API to allow the export of a metadatablock on this level, since it helps capturing custom settings.   

**What kind of user is the feature intended for?**

API Users

**Any brand new behavior do you want to add to Dataverse?**

* Extend Native API with a new endpoint `.../$collectionName/metadatablocks/$blockID`

**Use case**

The addition of this endpoint could allow [EasyDataverse](https://github.com/gdcc/easyDataverse) to connect to a specific Dataverse collection and build objects according to the custom settings given. For instance, if a user decides that an optional field of a metadata block should be required, this could be reflected onto the generated Python objects.

This would lead to an extension of the given `connect` method, that, when provided with a URL to a collection, fetches the specific metadata block definition:

```python
from easyDataverse import Dataset

dataset = Dataset.connect("https://demo.dataverse.org/my_dataverse")

# ... add metadata

# Uploads to the collection 
dataset.upload() 
```

Assuming a custom required field (e.g. grant number) is not given, upon trying to upload the dataset, a validation will be done, which results in a report on which fields are missing or wrong. For this [PyDantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev)`s validation capabilities would be used that result in such a message:

```python
ValidationError: 1 validation error for Citation
grant_number
  field required (type=value_error.missing)
```

Currently EasyDataverse needs to assume that every field is optional since the information is not given natively. Hence, this would be a valuable addition.

issues.title: Feature Request: Enhance Dataverse Caching for Dataset Version Summary
issues.body:
In order to speed up the getting of Dataset Version Differences/Summary a cache will be used.

Also see https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/issues/11503 for information regarding this ask.

Currently we have a CacheManager that handles the rate limiting data. This manager can be extended to cache json responses and store them in the Postgres database.

Some steps that need to be accomplished are:
1. create a table in the database to hold the json responses. 
CREATE IF NOT EXISTS UNLOGGED TABLE cache (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    value JSONB,
    created_at_utc TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

CREATE IF NOT EXISTS INDEX idx_cache_key ON cache (key);

2. Modify the CacheFactoryBean to include the json response cache (in memory as well as persisted in Postgres)
4. Define the key used to lookup the cache. User permission will determine what data is included in the response but the individual user id is not to be part of the key. The key needs to be limited so any user making this request will see the response that that would otherwise match the response based on their permissions.
5. Create feature flag or setting to enable/disable cache. Allow for future caching by having one setting that defines various caches (similar to the rate limiting setting). Could include cache size, TTL, enable/disable.
7. Invalidate the cache. Any update to the Dataset would need to invalid the cache.

9. Cache retrieval. Goes without saying, if cached in memory return it, if not, check db and if found return that. If not in memory or in db perform the actual code to generate the json and if caching enabled save json to memory and db.

issues.title: Performance: notification/unreadCount polling can fire multiple times per second
issues.body:
Description Summary from this [Slack thread](https://iqss.slack.com/archives/C010LA04BCG/p1790972249000629) 
**What steps does it take to reproduce the issue?**
1. Use the ModernUI in production while logged in.
2. Open and work with dataset pages during a normal curation workflow, such as reviewing and publishing/deleting draft datasets.
3. Monitor requests to `/api/v1/notifications/unreadCount` in the access logs or browser network panel.
4. In some cases, the page appears to start calling the endpoint repeatedly, multiple times per second.

- **When does this issue occur?**

  It appears intermittently during normal ModernUI usage.

   In one production example, a member of the curation team reviewed and published or deleted about 40 drafts throughout the day. That activity resulted in ~18,000 API calls, more than 11,000 of which were calls to `/api/v1/notifications/unreadCount`.

   Normally, notification polling appears to happen at a reasonable interval, but occasionally it seems to start firing continuously. One observed example showed 7 calls to `unreadCount` within the same second from the same dataset page/session.

- **Which page(s) does it occur on?**

  Observed on a ModernUI dataset page, for example:

  `/modern/datasets?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/PAYLYR&version=DRAFT`

  It is not yet clear whether this is limited to dataset pages or can happen anywhere the notification polling logic is active.

- **What happens?**

  `/api/v1/notifications/unreadCount` is sometimes requested multiple times per second instead of at the intended polling interval.

  This can result in a very large number of otherwise inexpensive API requests over a normal work session.

- **To whom does it occur (all users, curators, superusers)?**

  Observed for a curation-team user in production.

  It is not yet known whether this is role-specific or can affect any logged-in ModernUI user.

- **What did you expect to happen?**

  The unread notification count should be polled only at the configured/reasonable interval, with only one active polling loop per page/session.

  Navigating, re-rendering, or other component lifecycle events should not create overlapping polling loops or otherwise cause repeated calls multiple times per second.

Production ModernUI as of October 1, 2026.

issues.title: Feature Complete: Link Search
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets an authenticated user save the current filtered search on a collection as a "linked search," attaching it to one of their own collections so the search results surface there too (similar to linking a dataverse). The SPA's equivalent "Link" menu only offers "Link Collection" — the search-linking option is absent entirely. ## Legacy JSF behavior On any collection page, the "Link" dropdown offers a "Link Search" action that opens a "Link Search" dialog. The dialog lets the user pick one of their own collections and save the current search against it via "Save Linked Search". ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as a user who owns at least one collection. 2. Navigate to any collection page (e.g. a collection with sub-items). 3. Click the "Link" dropdown button near the top of the page, then click "Link Search". 4. Observe the "Link Search" dialog, which lets you choose "Your Dataverse" and click "Save Linked Search". ## New frontend behavior The equivalent "Link" dropdown on a collection page in the modern frontend only exposes "Link Collection". There is no "Link Search" entry, so the save-linked-search workflow cannot be started at all. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as the same user. 2. Navigate to the equivalent collection page. 3. Click the "Link" dropdown button. 4. Observe that only "Link Collection" is offered; there is no "Link Search" option. ## Expected behavior The Link menu on a collection page should include a "Link Search" option that opens an equivalent "save the current search" dialog, letting the user attach the search to one of their own collections. ## Current behavior The feature is entirely absent from the SPA — not even a placeholder/"Not Implemented" modal is shown, since there is no menu entry to click in the first place. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Link Search" dialog, reachable from Link -> Link Search on a collection page. ### New frontend Modern frontend "Link" dropdown showing only "Link Collection", with no search-linking option. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml (linkDataverseForm dialog), src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataversePage.java (saveSavedSearch(), linkMode) - New frontend source: no matching route/component found under src/router/routes.tsx or src/sections for this feature - Missing-items entry: "Dataverse Page - Save Linked Search" in DV - Missing items.md ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#546 ("Analysis and proposal for more customizable collection page") discusses displaying linked items on a customized collection page, but does not cover saving/creating a linked search. Not a duplicate. - No duplicate found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse, or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc after searching "save search", "linked search", and related terms. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The collection page's "Link" menu includes a "Link Search" option - [ ] Selecting it opens a dialog allowing the user to choose one of their own collections - [ ] Saving creates a linked search associated with that collection, matching legacy behavior - [ ] Covered by an automated or manual test verifying the linked search appears for the target collection

issues.title: Feature Complete: Support contact or User Guide link
issues.body: ## Summary Every legacy JSF page carries "User Guide" and "Support" links in the site header, and "Support" opens a contact form addressed to the installation's support address. The new frontend's header has neither — it shows only Language, Add Data and the user menu when signed in, or Language and Log In when anonymous. There is no way to reach installation support, or the user guide, from anywhere in the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverse_header.xhtml` renders "Add Data", "Search", "User Guide" and "Support" alongside the user menu. "Support" is a command link (`headerSupportLink`) that opens the shared contact dialog (`PF('contactForm').show()`), pre-addressed to installation support rather than to a specific collection. Both links appear on every page, including the account pages, and for anonymous visitors. ### Steps to observe 1. Open the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Observe "User Guide" and "Support" in the top-right header, on any page — including Account -> Account Information. 3. Click "Support" and observe the contact form for installation support. ## New frontend behavior `Header.tsx` renders the brand, a `LanguageSwitcher`, and then either `LoggedInHeaderActions` (Add Data + user menu) or a single OIDC "Log In" button. Nothing else. The SPA does have a contact modal, but it is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" reached from a collection's "Contact" button — that addresses the collection's contacts, not installation support, and it is not reachable from the account pages or from a dataset. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern), signed in or not. 2. Inspect the header: only Language, Add Data and the user menu (or Log In). 3. Go to `/modern/account?tab=accountInformation` and confirm there is no Support or User Guide link anywhere on the page. ## Expected behavior The new frontend should offer an installation-level support contact and a user-guide link that are reachable from any page, as legacy's header does — so a user who is stuck, or whose account details are wrong, has a route to ask for help. ## Current behavior Absent. The only contact affordance in the SPA is the per-collection "Email Collection Contact" modal, which has a different recipient and is not available from account or dataset pages. Users have no in-app path to installation support and no link to the documentation. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information page — note "User Guide" and "Support" in the header, present on every page. ### New frontend The same page in the SPA: header has only Language, Add Data and the user menu — no Support, no User Guide. (This capture also evidences #1125, the read-only account table.) ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (`headerSupportLink` opening `contactForm`, and the User Guide link), `header.support` and `header.guide` in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/Header.tsx) and [`LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) — no support or guide entry; the existing contact modal is [`src/sections/shared/contact/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/shared/contact) (collection-scoped) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information - Contact Support", and the related "Contact Support" rows under Login Page, ORCID Confirmation, OAuth Login Callback and Search Results in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - #1125 (Account Information is read-only) and #1120 (notification muting absent) are the sibling account-area gaps; a user hitting either has no support link to fall back on, which is part of why this one matters. - jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc#10 (no Sign Up entry in the header) is the other missing header affordance. - The collection-level contact form itself is fully implemented, including its math CAPTCHA — two rows of the missing-items list about that turned out to be wrong. This issue is specifically about an *installation* support route. - No issue covering a header support or user-guide link in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "contact support", "support link", "user guide link" and "header support" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] An installation support contact is reachable from any page in the new frontend - [ ] It addresses the installation's support address, distinct from a collection's contacts - [ ] A user guide link is available from the header, as in legacy - [ ] Both are available to anonymous visitors as well as signed-in users - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting both are present in the header

issues.title: Feature Complete: Notification settings pannel
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF can let users choose which notifications they receive, separately for email and in-app delivery, from a "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. **This panel is opt-in per installation: it only appears when an admin enables the `:ShowMuteOptions` database setting, which is `false` by default.** The new frontend's Notifications tab lists and dismisses notifications but has no muting controls, so on an installation that has turned muting on, users of the new frontend can't opt out of any notification type, including the emails. > [!IMPORTANT] > **You won't see this feature on a default installation.** The legacy panel is hidden unless `:ShowMuteOptions` is set to `true`. See [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf) below before trying to reproduce. ## Enabling the feature (legacy JSF) Notification muting is controlled by three installation-wide **database settings**. They're stored in the `setting` table, have no admin UI, and are managed through the admin settings API (usually only reachable from localhost or with the API unblock key): | Setting | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `:ShowMuteOptions` | `false` | When `true`, shows the "Notification settings" panel on the Notifications tab. When unset or `false`, the panel is not rendered at all. | | `:AlwaysMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types (e.g. `ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE`) that are always muted. Users can't turn them on. | | `:NeverMuted` | empty | Comma-separated notification types that are never muted. Users can't turn them off. | Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` or `:NeverMuted` show in the panel as greyed-out (disabled) checkboxes. If a type appears in both, `:AlwaysMuted` wins and a warning is logged. These settings were added in Dataverse 5.11. ```bash # Enable the panel curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Optional: lock some types so they show as disabled checkboxes curl -X PUT -d 'ASSIGNROLE,REVOKEROLE' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:AlwaysMuted curl -X PUT -d 'CREATEACC' http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:NeverMuted # Check the current value curl http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions # Revert to default (panel hidden) curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions ``` Docs: Installation Guide → [`:ShowMuteOptions`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#showmuteoptions), [`:AlwaysMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#alwaysmuted), [`:NeverMuted`](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/installation/config.html#nevermuted). User Guide → [Notifications](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/user/account.html#notifications). ## Legacy JSF behavior With `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, `dataverseuser.xhtml` renders a collapsible "Notification settings" panel above the notification list. It has two multi-select checkbox groups and a "Save Changes" button: - `notification.mutedEmails`: "Select the email notifications you wish to receive:" - `notification.mutedNotifications`: "Select the in-app notifications you wish to receive:" Unchecking a type mutes that notification for that delivery channel. Users can also manage the same preferences through the API: `GET /api/notifications/mutedEmails`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/notifications/mutedEmails/{typeName}`, and the same endpoints for `mutedNotifications`. ### Steps to observe 1. Enable the setting as a superuser: `curl -X PUT -d true http://localhost:8080/api/admin/settings/:ShowMuteOptions` (see [Enabling the feature](#enabling-the-feature-legacy-jsf)). 2. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Go to Account → Notifications (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=notifications`). 4. Expand "Notification settings". 5. You should see the two checkbox groups for email and in-app notification types. Uncheck one and click "Save Changes" to mute it. ## New frontend behavior The SPA Notifications tab (`/modern/account?tab=notifications`) shows "Displaying 1 - N of N Notifications", each row with a dismiss (X) control, plus a "Clear All Notifications" action. There is no settings panel and no muting UI, whatever the value of `:ShowMuteOptions`. A case-insensitive search for `mute` across `src/sections/account/notifications-section/` and `public/locales/en/account.json` finds nothing. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Enable `:ShowMuteOptions` on the backend as above. 2. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 3. Open the user menu and choose "Notifications" (or go to `/modern/account?tab=notifications`). 4. You'll see the notification list with dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", and no notification-settings or muting control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior When the installation has `:ShowMuteOptions=true`, users should be able to choose, per notification type, whether they get it by email and whether it appears in-app, the same way legacy's two checkbox groups work. The choice should be saved to their account. Types locked by `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` should be shown but not editable. When `:ShowMuteOptions` is false (the default), no muting UI should be shown, which matches legacy. ## Current behavior The SPA has no muting. On an installation with muting enabled, users can only dismiss notifications after they arrive. They can't stop unwanted notification emails without going back to the legacy JSF page or using the API. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF ### New frontend SPA Notifications tab: list with per-row dismiss and "Clear All Notifications", no notification-settings or muting panel. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: - [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml` L65–100](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml#L65-L100): the panel, gated by `jsf:rendered="#{settingsWrapper.showMuteOptions}"` - [`SettingsWrapper.java` L260–262](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/SettingsWrapper.java#L260-L262): `isShowMuteOptions()` defaults to `false`; also `isAlwaysMuted` / `isNeverMuted` - [`SettingsServiceBean.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/settings/SettingsServiceBean.java): `ShowMuteOptions`, `AlwaysMuted`, `NeverMuted` keys - [`DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/authorization/providers/builtin/DataverseUserPage.java): `toReceiveEmails`, `toReceiveNotifications`, `isDisabled` - API: [`api/Notifications.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/Notifications.java): `/api/notifications/mutedEmails[/{typeName}]` and `/api/notifications/mutedNotifications[/{typeName}]` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) and [`NotificationsHelper.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsHelper.tsx): no muting, and no `mute` strings in `public/locales/en/account.json` - Missing-items entries: "Notifications - Manage Muted Email Notifications" and "Notifications - Manage Muted In-App Notifications" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - #1125 (Account Information is read-only) is the related gap in the same account area. Both are about account self-service that the SPA shows but doesn't let the user change. - No issue covering notification muting in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc. Searched "muted notifications", "notification settings", "mute" and "notification preferences" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The notification settings UI is shown only when `:ShowMuteOptions` is `true` and is hidden by default - [ ] The Notifications tab offers per-type control over which notifications the user receives by email - [ ] It offers the same control for in-app notifications, separately from email - [ ] Types listed in `:AlwaysMuted` / `:NeverMuted` are shown as disabled and can't be changed - [ ] Choices are saved to the user's account and still show after a reload - [ ] Muting a type stops the email and/or the in-app entry for that type, depending on which channel was muted - [ ] Existing list, dismiss and "Clear All Notifications" behavior is unchanged - [ ] An automated test checks that a muted type is saved and that the UI is hidden when `:ShowMuteOptions` is false

issues.title: Feature Complete: Publish warning is incomplete
issues.body: ## Summary The new frontend handles the simple publish-blocked case correctly — a dataset whose immediate parent collection is unpublished gets legacy's exact "Would you like to publish both right now?" prompt. But it misses the other two cases legacy distinguishes: when **two generations** of ancestors are unpublished it still offers to publish "both", naming only the immediate parent; and when **a collection** whose parent is unpublished is published, the SPA shows a generic confirmation with no warning at all. ## Legacy JSF behavior Legacy has three distinct messages: | Case | Legacy string | | --- | --- | | Dataset, parent unpublished, user can publish it | `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" | | Dataset, **two** generations unpublished | `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} **and {1}** are published." | | Dataset, parent must be published by someone else | `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`: "This dataset cannot be published until {0} is published by its administrator." | And for collections: `dataverse.publish.failed` ("Cannot publish dataverse.") with `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` — "This dataverse cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Create an unpublished collection inside another unpublished collection, and a dataset inside the inner one. 3. Attempt to publish that dataset and observe the two-generations message naming both ancestors. 4. Attempt to publish the inner collection and observe the "cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published" notice. ## New frontend behavior **Two generations (dataset).** With `Root > QA Test Collection (unpublished) > Gap Review Subcollection 184 (unpublished) > dataset`, the SPA's Publish Dataset modal says only "This dataset cannot be published until **Gap Review Subcollection 184** is published. Would you like to publish both right now?" — the `.both` variant. It names one ancestor and offers to publish "both", although two ancestors are unpublished, so accepting cannot succeed as described. **Collection.** Publishing `Gap Review Subcollection 184`, whose parent `QA Test Collection` is unpublished, opens a Publish Collection modal reading only "Are you sure you want to publish your collection? Once you do so it must remain published." — no mention that the parent is unpublished and no equivalent of legacy's blocked-publish notice. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open the dataset at `/modern/datasets?persistentId=doi:10.5072/FK2/SSQN4W&version=DRAFT` (inside two unpublished collections). 3. Publish Dataset -> Publish, and observe the single-ancestor "publish both" wording. 4. Open `/modern/collections/gap-review-sub-184` and click Publish; observe the generic confirmation with no unpublished-parent warning. ## Expected behavior - A dataset with more than one unpublished ancestor should say so and name them, rather than offering to publish "both". - A dataset whose parent can only be published by someone else should say that, as legacy's `administrator` variant does. - Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished should warn, and either offer to publish the chain or explain why it cannot proceed — not present a plain confirmation. ## Current behavior Only the single-parent dataset case is handled. The other cases either show misleading wording (two generations) or no warning at all (collection), so a user can confirm an action whose stated effect is wrong. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: reproducing these states in legacy means publishing collections, which permanently changes install data, and the legacy flow was deliberately left untouched. The three dataset variants and the collection notice are quoted verbatim from `Bundle.properties` above. ### New frontend Two unpublished generations (`Root > QA Test Collection > Gap Review Subcollection 184 > dataset`), yet the modal names only the immediate parent and offers to publish "both": Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished — a generic confirmation with no warning: ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.mayNotPublish.both`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.twoGenerations`, `dataset.mayNotPublish.administrator`, `dataverse.publish.failed` and `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/publish-dataset/PublishDatasetModal.tsx) and [`PublishDatasetMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/PublishDatasetMenu.tsx); the collection side in [`src/sections/collection/publish-collection/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection/publish-collection) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Two Generations Unpublished" and "Dataverse Page - Blocked Publish Notice" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Dataset Page - Publish Blocked - Parent Unpublished" is **not** a gap: the SPA reproduces legacy's `.both` message word for word. Only the two-generations and collection variants are missing. - #1124 (curation status stubs) is the other finding from the same dataset publish menu. - No issue covering these publish-blocked variants was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "publish blocked", "cannot be published", "publish both" and "unpublished parent" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A dataset with two or more unpublished ancestors reports all of them and does not offer a "publish both" action that cannot succeed - [ ] A dataset whose ancestor must be published by another user gets the administrator variant of the message - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished warns before the confirmation, matching legacy's blocked-publish notice - [ ] The existing single-parent dataset case keeps its current wording and behavior - [ ] Covered by automated tests for the two-generations and collection cases

issues.title: Feature Complete: Publish Collection confirmation dialog bug.
issues.body: # Publishing a sub-collection with an unpublished parent shows a Continue/Cancel confirmation instead of legacy's blocked-publish notice ## Summary When a user publishes a collection whose parent collection is unpublished, legacy JSF blocks the action and explains why. The new frontend shows its normal publish confirmation with **Continue** and **Cancel**, as if publishing could succeed. This is a behavior mismatch, not just a missing warning. The SPA should block the action as legacy does, rather than add a warning to a confirmation that cannot succeed. ## Legacy JSF behavior | Key | Legacy string | |---|---| | `dataverse.publish.failed` | "Cannot publish dataverse." | | `dataverse.publish.failed.tip` | "This dataverse cannot be published because the dataverse it is in has not been published." | ### Steps to observe 1. Create an unpublished collection `A` under a published collection (for example, root). 2. Create a collection `B` inside `A`, and leave both unpublished. 3. Open `B` in the JSF UI and click **Publish**. 4. A dialog titled "Cannot publish dataverse." explains that the parent has not been published. It offers no option to continue publishing. ## New frontend behavior The SPA opens the generic publish modal on `/spa/collections/`: "Are you sure you want to publish your collection? Once you do so it must remain published." The modal has **Continue** and **Cancel** buttons. Nothing tells the user that the parent is unpublished. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use the same setup as above: collection `B` inside unpublished collection `A`. 2. Open `B` in the new frontend and click **Publish**. 3. The generic Continue/Cancel confirmation appears. 4. Click **Continue**. Result: [Needed: confirm whether the API error is shown, swallowed, or shown as a generic failure toast] ## Expected behavior - The SPA checks whether the parent collection is published before it shows the publish confirmation. - If the parent is unpublished, the SPA shows a blocking notice equivalent to `dataverse.publish.failed` / `dataverse.publish.failed.tip`, with only a close/OK action. - The SPA offers no **Continue** action and sends no publish request. - Collections with a published parent keep the current confirmation flow unchanged. ## Current behavior The SPA always shows the Continue/Cancel confirmation, whether or not the parent is published. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF ### New frontend ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF strings: `Bundle.properties`, https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties (`dataverse.publish.failed`, `dataverse.publish.failed.tip`) - New frontend collection publish: `src/sections/collection/publish-collection/`, https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection/publish-collection - New frontend use case: `src/collection/domain/useCases/publishCollection.ts` - Inventory entry: "Dataverse Page - Blocked Publish Notice" in `DV - Missing items.md` / `data/jsf-feature-inventory-MODEL 1.tsv:14` ## Related issues - #23: Publish-blocked warnings are incomplete. Closed, and moved to IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1121. It covers this case, but describes it as a missing *warning before confirmation*, not as the action being *blocked*. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1121: Feature Complete: Publish warning is incomplete. Its expected behavior allows "offering to publish the chain", which legacy does not do for collections. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#461 / PR #500: Publish Collection. Introduced the current Continue/Cancel modal. Its spec did not consider an unpublished parent. - No other issue covering this behavior was found in jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc or IQSS/dataverse-frontend (open or closed). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is unpublished shows a blocking notice that matches legacy's `dataverse.publish.failed` / `.tip` message. - [ ] That notice offers no Continue/publish action, and no publish API request is sent. - [ ] Publishing a collection whose parent is published keeps the existing Continue/Cancel confirmation. - [ ] Automated tests cover both the unpublished-parent and published-parent cases.

issues.title: Feature Complete: Curation status
issues.body: ## Summary This installation configures curation labels, and the new frontend correctly renders them: the dataset "Publish Dataset" menu shows a "Change Curation Status" submenu listing Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval and "Remove Current Status". Selecting any of them opens the "Not Implemented" modal instead of applying the status, so a curator cannot set, change or clear a dataset's curation status from the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior With curation labels configured, a curator can set a draft dataset's curation status from the dataset page, change it to another allowed label, or remove it. Legacy reports the outcome ("Curation Status Changed", "Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", "Curation Status Removed") and rejects invalid attempts with specific messages — label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, or the version already released (status can only be set on drafts). ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a **draft** dataset. 3. Set a curation status from the allowed labels, confirm the "Curation Status is now ..." confirmation, then remove it again. ## New frontend behavior `ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx` reads the allowed labels from the `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_STATUSES` setting and renders one item per label plus "Remove Current Status" — but every item is wired to the same handler: ```tsx const handleItemClick = (event: React.MouseEvent) => { event.stopPropagation() showModal() // useNotImplementedModal } ``` So the submenu is fully populated and looks functional, but each selection opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no curation-status history view either. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a draft dataset — this review used `doi:10.5072/FK2/Q9LZAD`. 3. Open the "Publish Dataset" dropdown and hover/open "Change Curation Status". 4. Select any label, for example "Privacy Review". 5. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal; the dataset's curation status is unchanged. ## Expected behavior A curator should be able to set a draft dataset's curation status to any allowed label, change it, and remove it from the new frontend, with the resulting status visible on the dataset and the legacy rejection cases handled (label not allowed, no change, labeling disabled, version already released). The status history should also be viewable, as legacy records it. ## Current behavior The submenu is present and correctly populated from configuration, which makes it look implemented, but every option opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Nothing is applied and no history is shown. This is more misleading than an absent control, because the labels render correctly. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Not screenshotted: setting a curation status changes real dataset state, and the legacy flow was left untouched deliberately. The behavior is established from the `dataset.curationstatus.*` bundle keys (`header`="Curation Status Changed", `info`="Curation Status is now \"{0}\"", `removed`="Curation Status Removed", plus the four failure cases) and from the fact that this installation's labels are configured — the SPA reads and displays them, as the screenshots below show. ### New frontend The populated "Change Curation Status" submenu on a draft dataset: Author Contacted, Privacy Review, Awaiting Paper Publication, Final Approval, and Remove Current Status. Selecting "Privacy Review" opens the "Not Implemented" modal, with the submenu still visible behind it. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: `dataset.curationstatus.*` keys in [`Bundle.properties`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties); API: `/api/datasets/$id/curationStatus` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/publish-dataset-menu/ChangeCurationStatusMenu.tsx) (every item calls `showModal()`), [`src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Change Curation Status", "Remove Curation Status" and "View Curation Status History" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - #1128, #1127 and #1126 are the other dataset-level controls stubbed with the same `NotImplementedModal`. Same pattern, different features. - The sibling "Submit for Review" control is stubbed the same way (`SubmitForReviewButton.tsx` has `onClick={showModal}`), but it only renders for a user who can update and **not** publish a dataset, so it could not be exercised with the single superuser account available here. Worth folding into the same work. - No issue covering curation-status management in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "curation status", "external status", "curation label" and "submit for review" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting a curation label applies it to the draft dataset instead of opening the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] The applied status is visible on the dataset - [ ] "Remove Current Status" clears it - [ ] Rejections are surfaced clearly: label not allowed, status unchanged, labeling disabled, and version already released - [ ] Curation status history can be viewed - [ ] The submenu only appears for users permitted to curate, and only for draft versions - [ ] Covered by automated tests for setting and removing a status

issues.title: Feature Complete: Account Information is read-only in the new frontend: no edit, password change or email verification
issues.body:
## Summary Legacy JSF lets a user manage their own account: edit their name, email, affiliation and position, change their password, and re-send the email-verification message when their address is unverified. The new frontend's Account Information tab is a **read-only table** — it displays the same fields but offers no edit, no password change and no email verification. The SPA source marks all three as TODO. ## Legacy JSF behavior `dataverseuser.xhtml` (Account Information tab) shows Username, Given Name, Family Name, Email, Affiliation and Position, with an "Edit Account" dropdown offering **Edit Account Information** and **Change Password**. An unverified address is flagged "Not Verified" beside a **Send Verification Email** button. The edit form saves or cancels. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Go to Account -> Account Information (`/dataverseuser.xhtml?selectTab=accountInfo`). 3. Observe the "Edit Account" dropdown and, next to the email, the "Not Verified" flag with "Send Verification Email". 4. Choose Edit Account Information, change a field and save or cancel; choose Change Password and set a new one. ## New frontend behavior `AccountInfoSection.tsx` renders a plain table of the session user's fields and nothing else. Its first lines are the SPA authors' own TODOs: ```tsx // TODO - Add verified email icon // TODO - Edit account information // TODO - Change password export const AccountInfoSection = () => { const { user } = useSession() return ({/* username, givenName, familyName, email, affiliation, position */}
) } ``` `public/locales/en/account.json` correspondingly has keys only for the field labels under `info.*` — there are no strings for editing, saving, cancelling, password change or email verification. The Notifications section likewise has no muting controls (no `mute` reference anywhere in `src/sections/account/notifications-section/`). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Open the user menu and choose "Account Information". 3. Observe the fields rendered as static text, with no Edit, Change Password or email-verification control anywhere on the tab. ## Expected behavior A user should be able to edit their own account details, change their password, and trigger email verification from the new frontend, with the unverified state visibly flagged — matching the legacy Account Information tab. ## Current behavior Read-only. The SPA shows account details but provides no way to change them; password changes and email verification must be done in the legacy JSF UI (or, for OIDC-backed accounts, in the identity provider). ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy Account Information tab: the "Edit Account" dropdown (Edit Account Information / Change Password) and the email flagged "Not Verified" with a "Send Verification Email" button. ### New frontend ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverseuser.xhtml), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseUserPage.java) (edit account, change password, `sendVerificationEmail`) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/account-info-section/AccountInfoSection.tsx) (read-only, with the TODOs quoted above), `public/locales/en/account.json` (`info.*` labels only), [`src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/account/notifications-section/NotificationsSection.tsx) (no muting) - Missing-items entries: "Account Information" rows (Edit Account Information, Save Account Changes, Change Password, Save New Password, Cancel Edit, Verify Email Address) in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#712 ("SPA User Menu Navigation Breaks After Visiting Account Information", closed) touched this same tab but concerned navigation, not editing. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#1020 ("Redesign the Dataverse account creation workflow to encourage users to add ORCIDs") and #1022 ("Let a user add a ROR to describe their affiliation during account creation") both propose changes to account *creation*; they assume account details are editable. Related, not duplicates. - For OIDC-backed installations, password change belongs to the identity provider (see IQSS/dataverse-frontend#652, closed, which established that the SPA delegates login to a themed Keycloak page). Scoping this issue should decide whether "Change Password" is in scope for the SPA at all, or whether it should link out to the provider. - No issue covering editable account information in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "edit account information SPA", "change password SPA", "account information" and "verify email SPA" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A user can edit their given name, family name, email, affiliation and position from the Account Information tab - [ ] Changes are saved, and Cancel discards them without saving - [ ] An unverified email address is visibly flagged and a verification email can be re-sent - [ ] A password change is offered for builtin accounts, or the tab links to the identity provider where that is the correct owner — whichever the maintainers decide, the current silent absence is resolved - [ ] Covered by automated tests for editing and saving account details

issues.title: Feature Complete: Dataset and file permissions management
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a dataset curator manage who can access a dataset and its restricted files: assign and remove roles on the dataset, and — on a separate file-permissions screen — grant or reject file access requests (individually or in bulk), revoke granted access, and review the request history. In the new frontend the dataset Edit menu still shows a "Permissions" submenu with "Dataset" and "File" entries, but both are wired to the shared not-implemented handler, so neither screen is reachable. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **Dataset** opens `permissions-manage.xhtml`, which lists the users and groups with access, their roles, an "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" action and a "Remove Assigned Role" action per row, plus a Roles panel. Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> **File** opens `permissions-manage-files.xhtml`, which lists restricted files and pending access requests with: Grant Access, Grant All / Grant Selected, Reject All / Reject Selected, Revoke access for an already-granted user, toggles to show deleted files and the access-request history, and a download of the file-permissions history. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset, then Edit Dataset -> Permissions -> Dataset (or `/permissions-manage.xhtml?id=`). 3. Observe the Users/Groups table with "Assign Roles to Users/Groups" and "Remove Assigned Role". 4. Choose Permissions -> File (`/permissions-manage-files.xhtml?id=`) and observe the file-access request and grant controls. ## New frontend behavior `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx` renders the submenu and attaches the not-implemented handler to the whole dropdown: ```tsx {dataset.permissions.canManageDatasetPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.dataset')})} {dataset.permissions.canManageFilesPermissions && ( {t('...permissions.file')})} ``` So selecting either "Dataset" or "File" opens the "Not Implemented" modal. There is no dataset-permissions or file-permissions route or component in the SPA. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Open a dataset you can administer and open the "Edit Dataset" dropdown. 3. Open the "Permissions" submenu and select "Dataset" (then repeat for "File"). 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal in both cases. ## Expected behavior A dataset curator should be able to manage dataset role assignments in the new frontend (list, assign, remove) and handle file access requests (grant or reject individually and in bulk, revoke granted access, review and export the request history, and optionally show deleted files) — gated on `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` respectively. ## Current behavior Both submenu entries are present but non-functional — they open the generic "Not Implemented" modal. Dataset access administration requires leaving the SPA for the legacy JSF pages. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy dataset Permissions page for a draft test dataset: Users/Groups with their roles, "Assign Roles to Users/Groups", and "Remove Assigned Role" per assignment. **Scope note:** the *file* permissions screen could not be shown with meaningful content. It lists restricted files and access requests, and no data file can exist in this install — its only storage driver is `s3`, pointed at AWS with placeholder credentials and no S3 service running, so every upload fails. The file-side controls are therefore described from `permissions-manage-files.xhtml` rather than screenshotted. ### New frontend The shared "Not Implemented" modal that both entries open. **Note:** this capture was taken from the *collection* Edit dropdown, which uses the same `NotImplementedModal` component that `EditDatasetPermissionsMenu`'s `showModal` triggers. The SPA session expired partway through this review and re-authenticating requires a password, so a capture from the dataset Permissions submenu specifically is pending; the wiring is quoted above. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/permissions-manage-files.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/roles-assign.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/dataset/dataset-action-buttons/edit-dataset-menu/EditDatasetPermissionsMenu.tsx) (`onSelect={showModal}`); no permissions route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entries: "Dataset Page - Manage Dataset Permissions", "Dataset Page - Manage File Permissions" and the nine "Manage File Permissions" rows in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - #1136 (collection "Manage Permissions" opens placeholder) is the collection-level counterpart, stubbed the same way. Same pattern, different object. - #1127 (Private/Preview URL creation) and #1128 (Thumbnails + Widgets) are sibling entries in the same dataset Edit menu. - IQSS/dataverse#12076 ("Dataverse linking still requires superuser despite introduction of LinkDataverse permission") concerns permission semantics rather than this UI. Not a duplicate. - No issue covering SPA dataset or file permission management was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "dataset permissions SPA", "file access requests", "grant file access" and "manage permissions" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Permissions -> Dataset opens a role-assignment view instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] Roles can be assigned to users and groups, and existing assignments removed - [ ] Permissions -> File opens a file-access view listing restricted files and pending requests - [ ] Access requests can be granted and rejected individually and in bulk - [ ] Granted access can be revoked - [ ] The access-request history can be reviewed and exported, and deleted files optionally shown - [ ] The two entries respect `canManageDatasetPermissions` and `canManageFilesPermissions` - [ ] Covered by automated tests for assigning a role and for granting and rejecting a file access request

issues.title: Feature Complete: Dashboard Harvesting Client

API: `/api/harvest/clients` - New frontend source: no harvesting route or component found — nothing under `src/sections` for harvesting, no harvesting route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts); the only `harvest` matches are [`src/sections/homepage/metrics/MetricsResults.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/homepage/metrics/MetricsResults.tsx) and the Dataverse Hub metric mappers - Missing-items entries: "Harvesting Clients" rows (Create steps 1-4, Run Harvest Now, Edit, Save, Delete, Cancel dialog, Navigate Wizard Steps) in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - #1135 (SPA has no dashboard or dashboard entry point) is the blocking prerequisite — legacy reaches this page from the dashboard's Harvesting Clients card. - #1134 (dashboard Move Dataset workflow absent) is the sibling dashboard-tool gap. - No issue covering harvesting administration in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "harvest", "manage harvesting", "harvesting clients UI SPA", "harvesting server OAI SPA" and "OAI set" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A superuser can reach a harvesting-clients view in the new frontend - [ ] The view lists configured clients with their schedule and last-harvest status - [ ] A client can be created with nickname, OAI server URL, target local collection, metadata format, schedule and display settings - [ ] The creation flow validates required fields and can be cancelled without creating a client - [ ] An existing client can be edited, deleted, and harvested on demand - [ ] The view is not reachable by non-superusers - [ ] Covered by automated tests for creating, editing and deleting a client

issues.title: Feature Complete: Dashboard Harvesting Server
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF gives superusers a "Manage Harvesting Server" page that turns this installation's OAI-PMH server on or off and defines the OAI sets (search-query-defined collections of local datasets) that remote harvesters can pull. issues.title: Feature Complete: Downloads metrics panel
issues.body: ## Summary The legacy collection page shows a usage-metrics panel — a "Metrics" toggle with the collection's download count — directly above the collection description. The new frontend's collection page has no metrics panel at all. The SPA does show metrics on its homepage, but those come from Dataverse Hub (aggregate, cross-installation figures), not from this collection, so no collection-level usage metric is available anywhere in the SPA. ## Legacy JSF behavior On a collection page, a small panel renders at the top-left with a "Metrics" label and the download total for that collection ("0 Downloads" on a fresh install). It sits beside the Contact / Share / Edit actions and is visible to anonymous visitors as well as editors. ### Steps to observe 1. Open the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Navigate to the root collection at `/dataverse/root`. 3. Observe the "Metrics | 0 Downloads" panel above the collection description. ## New frontend behavior The SPA collection page renders the breadcrumb, title, description, Contact / Share actions, the search box and the items panel — but no metrics panel. There is no collection-level metrics component: `src/sections/collection/` contains no metrics module, and the only metrics code, `src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx`, is homepage-only and sourced from `useGetInstallationMetrics` via `dataverseHubRepository` (Dataverse Hub aggregate data, which is why a fresh local install displays figures like 304K datasets and 170M downloads). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to the root collection at `/modern/collections/root`. 3. Observe that no metrics or download count appears anywhere on the page — only Contact and Share beside the title. ## Expected behavior The collection page in the new frontend should show that collection's usage metrics — at minimum the download count legacy shows — sourced from the installation's own metrics for that collection rather than from aggregate Hub data. ## Current behavior Absent. No collection-level metrics panel exists in the SPA. The homepage metrics block is unrelated: it reports cross-installation Dataverse Hub aggregates, not this collection's usage. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy root collection page: the "Metrics | 0 Downloads" panel is visible above the description, beside Contact / Share / Edit. ### New frontend Modern frontend root collection page, same collection and window size: only Contact and Share — no metrics panel and no download count. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse.xhtml) (collection metrics panel), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseServiceBean.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/DataverseServiceBean.java), `/api/info/metrics/downloads` family - New frontend source: no collection metrics component found under [`src/sections/collection/`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/tree/develop/src/sections/collection); the only metrics code is [`src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/homepage/metrics/Metrics.tsx) with `useGetInstallationMetrics` / `dataverseHubRepository`, which is homepage-scoped and Hub-sourced - Missing-items entry: "Dataverse Page - View Root Dataverse Download Metrics" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#474 ("Feature Request/Idea: Dataverse metrics bar at sub-dataverse level") asks to extend usage metrics to sub-collections, and explicitly notes that Dataverse "already provides download and Make Data Count metrics in the GUI at the installation/top-level collection level". It presupposes the top-level collection metrics this issue reports as missing from the SPA, so it depends on this rather than duplicating it. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#779 ("Show MDC metrics in SPA Dataset page") is the dataset-level counterpart. Same theme, different object; not a duplicate. - No issue reporting the absent collection-level metrics panel in the SPA was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "collection metrics downloads", "dataverse metrics panel SPA", "collection downloads count" and "installation metrics homepage" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The collection page in the new frontend shows that collection's download count - [ ] The figure reflects the installation's own metrics for that collection, not Dataverse Hub aggregates - [ ] It is visible to anonymous visitors, as in legacy - [ ] It renders sensibly at zero ("0 Downloads") and while loading - [ ] Covered by an automated test asserting the collection metric renders ## Notes - This still need to be configured [:MetricsUrl](https://guides.dataverse.org/en/6.12.1/installation/config.html#id534) - The data currently displayed on the JSF version is an accurate number, this will change due the API being changed and report the same number than the API.

A superuser must fall back to the legacy JSF UI to reach any dashboard function. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy header user dropdown for a superuser, showing the "Dashboard" entry between dividers, with the destination `/dashboard.xhtml` page and its administrative cards visible behind it. ### New frontend Modern frontend header user dropdown for the same superuser, listing only My Data, Notifications, Account Information, API Token and Log Out — the Dashboard entry is absent. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dataverse_header.xhtml) (superuser-gated `h:outputLink` to `/dashboard.xhtml`), [`src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/dashboard.xhtml) (the dashboard cards), `header.dashboard` in `src/main/java/propertyFiles/Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: no dashboard route or component found — [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) has no dashboard route, [`src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/layout/header/LoggedInHeaderActions.tsx) renders the user dropdown with no superuser branch, and no `dashboard` string exists under `public/locales/en/` - Missing-items entry: "Site Header - Go to Dashboard" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#258 ("admin dashboard: allow graphical creation of builtin users") requests a new capability on the dashboard's Manage Users page; it presupposes the dashboard exists rather than tracking its absence in the SPA. issues.title: Feature Complete: 403, 500 and other error pages
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF serves three distinct error pages, mapped by status code in `web.xml`: a 403 that tells the user they are not authorized and links them to installation support, a 500 that identifies an internal server error, and a 404. The new frontend differentiates only the 404 case; every other routing or loader failure renders one generic page reading "Oops, something went wrong..." with no status code, no indication of whether the problem is permissions or a server fault, and no support contact. ## Legacy JSF behavior `WEB-INF/web.xml` maps `403 -> /403.xhtml`, `500 -> /500.xhtml` and `404 -> /404static.xhtml`. - **403** renders "**Not Authorized** - You are not authorized to view this page. If you believe this is an error, please contact Support for assistance.", where the support name is a mailto/contact link. - **500** renders "**Internal Server Error** - An unexpected error was encountered, no more information is available." ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080). 2. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/403.xhtml and observe the Not Authorized message with its support contact link. 3. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/500.xhtml and observe the Internal Server Error message. ## New frontend behavior The SPA has exactly one differentiated error page — `NotFoundPage` at `/404` (`Route.NOT_FOUND_PAGE`), which correctly reports "We can't find the ... you're looking for." Everything else is handled by a single `errorElement`: `ErrorPage` is attached to the root route and to each child route in `src/router/routes.tsx`, and it renders only the strings from `public/locales/en/errorPage.json`: ```json { "message": { "heading": "Oops,", "errorText": "something went wrong..." }, "brandName": "Dataverse", "backToHomepage": "Back to {{brandName}} Homepage" } ``` There is no 403 route, no 500 route, and `ErrorPage` does not read the status from the route error — it ignores `useRouteError()`'s status entirely except for logging. So a permission failure and a server fault are visually indistinguishable to the user, and neither offers a support contact. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern). 2. Navigate to any unknown path, for example http://localhost:8000/modern/dashboard/move-dataset, and observe that a 404 *is* handled (redirect to `/modern/404`). 3. Inspect `src/sections/Route.enum.ts` and confirm the only error route is `NOT_FOUND_PAGE = '/404'` — there is no 403 or 500 equivalent. 4. Inspect `src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx` and `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` and confirm the generic page carries no status code and no support link. ## Expected behavior A permission failure in the new frontend should render a 403-equivalent page that says the user is not authorized and points them at installation support, and an unexpected server error should render a 500-equivalent page that identifies it as a server error — rather than both collapsing into "Oops, something went wrong...". ## Current behavior Divergent, not entirely absent: the SPA handles 404 properly but has no 403 or 500 variants. Both conditions fall through to one generic error page that omits the status code, the permission-versus-server distinction, and the support contact that legacy provides on 403. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy 403 page: names the authorization problem and links to installation support. Legacy 500 page: identifies the failure as an internal server error. ### New frontend The SPA's only status-specific error page is the 404 shown below. **This is not the 403/500 path** — it is included to show that error pages exist but only for the not-found case. The generic `ErrorPage` that a 403 or 500 would produce could not be triggered on demand in a dev build, so its content is quoted above directly from `ErrorPage.tsx` and `errorPage.json` rather than screenshotted. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml) (`error-page` mappings), [`src/main/webapp/403.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/403.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/500.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/500.xhtml) - New frontend source: [`src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/error-page/ErrorPage.tsx) (generic, status-agnostic), [`src/router/routes.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/router/routes.tsx) (`errorElement: ` on every route), [`src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-found-page/NotFoundPage.tsx), `public/locales/en/errorPage.json` - Missing-items entries: "Error Pages - 403 Forbidden Page" and "Error Pages - 500 Internal Server Error Page" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - The sibling row "Error Pages - 404 Static Fallback Page" is **not** a gap: the SPA's `NotFoundPage` covers it. The only residual difference is that legacy's `404static.xhtml` is served by the application server while the SPA's 404 is a client-side route needing the JS bundle. - No issue covering SPA 403 or 500 error pages was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "403", "500", "error page", "forbidden" and "internal server error" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A permission failure renders a 403-equivalent page stating the user is not authorized - [ ] The 403 page offers a way to contact installation support, as legacy does - [ ] An unexpected server error renders a 500-equivalent page identifying it as a server error - [ ] The generic fallback distinguishes these cases rather than showing the same text for all failures - [ ] The existing 404 behavior is unchanged - [ ] Covered by automated tests asserting the 403 and 500 states render their respective pages ## Notes I am not sure if these are all the codes that need to be handled or if the SPA has another mechanism of escape for these other error codes.

issues.title: Feature Complete: Collection "Manage Groups"

In the SPA, the Edit menu's "Groups" shortcut is present but non-functional, following the same pattern as the "Permissions" shortcut. ## Legacy JSF behavior Edit -> Groups navigates to a working "Manage Dataverse Groups" page with explanatory content ("Why Use Groups?", "How To Use Groups") and a "Create Group" action. ### Steps to observe 1. Observe the working "Manage Dataverse Groups" page with a "Create Group" button. ## New frontend behavior Edit -> Groups opens the same generic "Not Implemented" modal used elsewhere in the SPA, instead of a groups-management view. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal instead of a groups page. ## Expected behavior Selecting "Groups" from the Edit menu should load a working groups-management view equivalent to the legacy page, including the ability to create a group. ## Current behavior The menu item exists but only opens the placeholder "Not Implemented" modal - no groups-management UI has been implemented. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Manage Dataverse Groups" page reached via Edit -> Groups, with a "Create Group" action. ### New frontend Modern frontend showing the "Not Implemented" modal after clicking Edit -> Groups. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: src/main/webapp/manage-groups.xhtml - New frontend source: src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx is shown in place of a real groups route - Missing-items entry: "Dataverse Page - Manage Groups Shortcut" in DV - Missing items.md ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#830 and #831 (group-creation bug reports) - a maintainer comment on #830 confirms "the related SPA page hasn't been implemented yet," directly corroborating this finding.
