issues.title: Feature Complete: Collection "Theme + Widgets"
issues.body: ## Summary Legacy JSF lets a collection administrator brand a collection from the "Theme + Widgets" page: inherit the parent theme, upload logo / thumbnail / footer images, set header background, link and text colors, and set a tagline and website link. The new frontend keeps the "Theme + Widgets" entry in the collection Edit menu, but selecting it opens the "Not Implemented" modal — no theme form exists in the SPA, so collection branding cannot be viewed or changed there. ## Legacy JSF behavior `ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml` renders a two-tab page ("Theme" and "Widgets"). The Theme tab is bound to `themeWidgetFragment.editDv` and exposes the full branding form. It renders for any collection that has a parent, and for the root collection unless the `rootDataverseThemeDisabled` setting is on. ### Steps to observe 1. Log into the legacy JSF app (http://localhost:8080) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to a non-root collection — for example "QA Test Collection" at `/dataverse/qa-test-collection`. 3. Click the "Edit" dropdown, then "Theme + Widgets" (`/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml?id=2`). 4. Observe the "Theme" tab with: Inherit Theme checkbox, Logo Image upload, Thumbnail Image upload, Header Colors (Background Color, Link Color, Text Color), Tagline, Website, Footer Image upload, and "Save Changes" / "Cancel". ## New frontend behavior The collection Edit dropdown still lists "Theme + Widgets", but the item is wired to the shared not-implemented handler rather than to a route: in `EditCollectionDropdown.tsx` it is a `DropdownButtonItem` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`, which opens `NotImplementedModal`. The modal offers a link back to the original JSF page as the only way to use the feature. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Log into the modern frontend (http://localhost:8000/modern) as `dataverseAdmin`. 2. Navigate to the same collection at `/modern/collections/qa-test-collection`. 3. Click the "Edit" dropdown and select "Theme + Widgets". 4. Observe the "Not Implemented" modal: "This feature is not implemented yet in the Modern version. If you want to use this feature you can go to the original Dataverse page." No theme form is shown. ## Expected behavior Selecting "Theme + Widgets" for a collection should open a theme/branding form in the SPA equivalent to the legacy Theme tab, letting an administrator inherit the parent theme or set the collection's logo, thumbnail and footer images, header colors, tagline and website, and save those changes. ## Current behavior The menu entry is present but non-functional: it opens the generic "Not Implemented" modal instead of a theme form. There is no theme route or component in the SPA, so the only path to collection branding is to leave the SPA for the legacy JSF page. ## Evidence ### Legacy JSF Legacy "Theme" tab for QA Test Collection, showing the full branding form (Inherit Theme, Logo Image, Thumbnail Image, Header Colors, Tagline, Website, Footer Image) and the sibling "Widgets" tab. ### New frontend Modern frontend: selecting "Theme + Widgets" from the collection Edit dropdown (visible behind the modal) opens the "Not Implemented" modal. ## Implementation references - Legacy JSF source: [`src/main/webapp/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/ThemeAndWidgets.xhtml), [`src/main/webapp/themeAndWidgetsFragment.xhtml`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/webapp/themeAndWidgetsFragment.xhtml) (`p:tab id="themeTab"`), [`src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/ThemeWidgetFragment.java`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/develop/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/ThemeWidgetFragment.java) (`initEditDv`), `dataverse.theme.*` keys in `Bundle.properties` - New frontend source: [`src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/collection/edit-collection-dropdown/EditCollectionDropdown.tsx) renders `editCollection.themeAndWidgets` with `onClick={handleNotImplementedClick}`; [`src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/not-implemented/NotImplementedModal.tsx); no theme route in [`src/sections/Route.enum.ts`](https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/blob/develop/src/sections/Route.enum.ts) - Missing-items entry: "Theme & Widgets - View Theme Tab" in `DV - Missing items.md` ## Related issues - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#268 ("Support collection logo image") asks for logo customization via the Native API and states the new SPA UI should retain collection logo customization. It overlaps on the logo image only, not the rest of the theme form (inherit theme, colors, tagline, website, thumbnail and footer images). Closely related — worth coordinating, but narrower than this gap. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#298 ("Dataverse collection thumbnail in addition to Logo Image as banner (SPA)") proposes a new, distinct thumbnail field on the Theme and Widgets page. It extends the theme form rather than tracking its absence. Not a duplicate. - IQSS/dataverse-frontend#514 ("More personalizable collections - Analysis", closed as completed) was the analysis for more personalizable SPA collections; it did not deliver the theme form. Background context. - IQSS/dataverse#12669 ("Uploading an Image resets the Dataverse Collection Theme form") is a bug in the legacy theme form. Unrelated to the SPA gap, but confirms the legacy form is the reference behavior. - No issue tracking the missing SPA theme form was found in IQSS/dataverse-frontend, IQSS/dataverse or jp-tosca/dv-modern-fc, searching "theme", "theme widgets", "branding", "collection theme customization", "logo upload collection" and "tagline" across open and closed items. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Selecting "Theme + Widgets" for a collection opens a theme form in the SPA instead of the "Not Implemented" modal - [ ] The form supports inheriting the parent collection's theme - [ ] The form supports uploading and removing the logo, thumbnail and footer images, with the legacy type and size validation - [ ] Once a logo is present, the form offers the Logo Format choice (Square / Rectangle), and for Rectangle the Logo Alignment (Left / Center / Right) and Logo Background Color - [ ] Once a footer image is present, the form offers its alignment and background color - [ ] The form supports setting header background, link and text colors - [ ] The form supports setting a tagline (140 characters or fewer) and a website link - [ ] Saving persists the theme and it is reflected on the collection page; Cancel discards changes - [ ] The entry is only offered to users permitted to edit the collection - [ ] Covered by an automated test for saving and for inheriting a theme

issues.title: Feature Request: Sign up builtin users via API, with optional ORCID iD
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to the Dataverse Project through the creation of a feature request!

More information on ideas/feature requests and contributions can be found in the "Contributing to Dataverse" page:
https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/contributor/index.html

Please fill out as much of the template as you can.
Start below this comment section.
-->

**Overview of the Feature Request**
Let new users create a builtin Dataverse account through the API, so the modern UI (SPA) can offer a "Sign Up" page like the JSF one. While signing up, users can optionally connect their ORCID iD. ORCID then pre-fills their details (name, email, affiliation, position and a suggested username), and the ORCID iD is saved to the new account.


**What kind of user is the feature intended for?**
(Example users roles: API User, Curator, Depositor, Guest, Superuser, Sysadmin)
- Guest: a new user creating an account.
- API User: front ends such as the SPA that call the new endpoints.
- Sysadmin: turns the feature on and configures ORCID and the allowed redirect URLs.

**What inspired the request?**
Modern UI Feature Compleness
[Modern UI Sign-Up with ORCID - Design Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1z2jQO5_bUu-kKQZ2h3ElTsmsf1C0ArG151QJ7R7tSoo/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.9vxakxeugg0c)


**What existing behavior do you want changed?**

- ORCID records from API v3.0: affiliation and position aren't found at all, because the parser only understands the v2 format. This also affects "Log In with ORCID".
- When a record has several employments, Dataverse takes the first one listed. It should take the current one: no end date, and the latest start date.


**Any brand new behavior do you want to add to Dataverse?**
- `POST /api/users/signup` creates a builtin user:
  - It uses the same validation as the JSF "Sign Up" page and respects `:AllowSignUp`.
  - It's rate-limited per client IP address.
- `GET /api/users/signup/orcid/authorize` and `POST /api/users/signup/orcid` connect an ORCID iD before the account exists:
  - They return the user's ORCID details, including the affiliation's ROR ID when ORCID has one.
  - They also return a short-lived token that the sign-up request uses to save the ORCID iD.
- `GET /api/users/:me` includes `authenticatedOrcid`.
- New settings:
  - `dataverse.feature.api-builtin-user-signup`: feature flag, off by default.
  - `dataverse.api.signup.rate-limit-per-hour`
  - `dataverse.api.signup.orcid-redirect-uris`

**Any open or closed issues related to this feature request?**
https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse-frontend/issues/1049

**Are you thinking about creating a pull request for this feature?**  
Help is always welcome, is this feature something you or your organization plan to implement?
